From the evidence before us relating to the initial step in our economic evaluation - the alignment of urban area activity - it is fair to say that there has been a dramatic increase in suburban residential and commercial activity since the development of our existing commercial zone regulations. The population statistics certainly highlight the demographic shifts since World War II. The comparative statistics indicate that the urban fringe is overtaking the central city in commercial importance, at least with respect to many types of business and industry. The next step in our investigation is to perceive the degree of interrelationship, if any, which exists between the central city and the intensified economic and social activity of the suburbs.
INTERRELATIONSHIP OF CITY & SUBURB:
We were persuaded at the interim stage of this proceeding that there is a substantial connection between the industrial parks and commercial establishments of the suburbs and the economic, business, and social life of the center city.
